messages.author: 9f062cd8f5597556
messages.subject: odd temperature predictions for Austral summer
parts:
Hi everyone,

My name is Pablo Garcia-Diaz, and I am a post-doc working on ecosystem services and modelling forest dynamics in northern Argentina. I am using NicheMapR to obtain microclimate predictions for my study sites. I am comparing mcera5 and the 'micro_era5' function predictions with data-logger (10-cm belowground) data to assess the fit of the 'micro_era5' predictions. I have access to validation data for high mountains (4500 masl; 4 sites) and sub-tropical forest environments (700 masl; 1 site). To obtain predictions, I am running the 'micro_era5' models with and without the snow model, including LAI estimates, and running the models with soilgrids = 0 and IR = 2. I am averaging the no-snow and the snow model predictions for 0, 2.5, 5, and 10-cm to account for landslides, rodent activity, etc. I am also comparing the individual predictions for each depth. So far, the performance has been impressive, with R^2 scores ranging between 0.6 and 0.98.

However, a closer inspection of the RMSE scores indicates that my 'micro_era5' predictions show a U-pattern along the months of the year, as you can see in the graphs below. I thought it was a curious, consistent pattern across all five sites and two environments. I was wondering if anyone would have any insights into why this might be happening.

Graph: RMSE scores for the high mountain (black dots) and subtropical forest (pink dots) models.

Two example plots showing the predicted (red) and recorded (black) temperatures at the subtropical forest site:

December 2021

July 2022 (winter)


I am likely making a mistake somewhere, but I have run the models with different settings, and they tend to yield similar results. Any tips or suggestions will be more than welcome.

Cheers

Pablo

messages.author: 6cec8ea3702ece93
messages.subject: Re: odd temperature predictions for Austral summer
parts:
Hi Pablo,

Looks like you were making predictions in full sun (0% shade - the default setting for the minimum shade scenario, which is what is outputted to the 'soil' output in the list returned from micro_era5) but your site is in a forest. The default maximum shade is 90% and results for soil temperature under this scenario can be found in the output table 'shadsoil'. I tried running your site with the 'soil_ncep' shiny app and got the plot below for 0 cm and 10 cm in 90% shade. Be sure to run at least 6 months 'spin up' prior to the time period of interest as well, so that the initial conditions (esp. soil moisture) have little impact on the predictions. It might be worth going through the vignette on the microclimate model if you haven't already. I'm not sure how relevant snow is to your site - does it ever snow?


All the best,
Mike
